responsibility: This module is GNARL, the low-level Ada tasking runtime support library used by GCC’s Ada front end to implement the language’s concurrency and real-time execution model on top of host operating-system primitives. Its responsibility is to bridge Ada tasking semantics to platform services such as threads, condition variables, clocks, timed waits, and related synchronization/runtime facilities, providing the portability layer that insulates higher-level Ada runtime code from target-specific details. The file set in this module commonly consists of small support shims and runtime helpers; for example, thread-support code handles pthread condition-variable clock selection and clock-resolution queries so Ada timed operations follow GNAT’s chosen tasking clock even on systems with nonuniform POSIX support. Overall, this module is the Ada runtime subsystem concerned with task execution, scheduling-related timing, and OS interface support rather than front-end parsing, semantic analysis, or generic code generation.
